layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Medical image segmentation enables doctors to observe lesion regions better and make accurate diagnostic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decisions. Single-branch models such as U-Net have achieved great progress in this field. However, the com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plementary local and global pathological semantics of heterogeneous neural networks have not yet been fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explored. The class-imbalance problem remains a serious issue. To alleviate these two problems, we propose a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: novel model called BCU-Net, which leverages the advantages of ConvNeXt in global interaction and U-Net in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: local processing. We propose a new multilabel recall loss (MRL) module to relieve the class imbalance problem

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and facilitate deep-level fusion of local and global pathological semantics between the two heterogeneous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branches. Extensive experiments were conducted on six medical image datasets including retinal vessel and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polyp images. The qualitative and quantitative results demonstrate the superiority and generalizability of BCU-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Net. In particular, BCU-Net can handle diverse medical images with diverse resolutions. It has a flexible structure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: owing to its plug-and-play characteristics, which promotes its practicality.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Medical image segmentation has been used to identify clinically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: valuable lesions in medical images. For example, accurate vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boundaries, definite lesion areas, and complete anatomy segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are crucial for the clinical assessment of various diseases, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: glaucoma [1], diabetic retinopathy [2], prostate [3], polyps [4,5], brain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tumors [6], and other maladies [7–11]. More automated medical image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation systems have been proposed to provide a firm reference

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the quantification of disease progression. These systems can assist

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: doctors in their actual diagnostic work more positively and efficiently,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: including measuring the size or shape of the human brain, completing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: targeted treatments, and implementing imaging-guided interventions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hence, with the rapid development of artificial intelligence, medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image segmentation tools have become an important part of modern

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: healthcare and have attracted increasing attention. Recently, deep

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neural networks have been used to construct medical image segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion models. Various novel models such as U-Net [12], DeepLab V3+

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [13], SegNet [14], RefineNet [15], and PSPNet [16] have achieved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accurate segmentation of diverse medical images for clinical diagnosis.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Among all the models, U-Net [12] has shown much greater potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for different segmentation tasks [17,18]. U-Net and its model variants

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been successfully used for the segmentation tasks of the liver [19,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 20], heart [21], skin lesions [22], colon histology [23,24], retinal vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [25–27], polyps [28,29], and prostate [30]. U-Net consists of an encoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a decoder. The encoder implements continuous down-sampling of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the input medical image, focusing on the corresponding pathological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: details. By contrast, the decoder completes continuous upsampling,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which generates the final segmentation result. The encoder-decoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure provides a firm foundation for subsequent research. Howev-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: er, U-Net and its variants may lose global or multiscale pathological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information because of the use of small convolutions. Consequently,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: numerous emerging technologies such as pyramid-scale aggregation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: blocks [31], hard attention networks [32], gate attention mechanisms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [33], atrous convolution [34], multi-scale aggregation blocks [35], a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: combination of high- and low-frequency information [36], and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fusion of spatial and contextual paths [37] have been proposed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: address this problem. Recently, transformers have shown remarkable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: advantages in global relationship modeling. Hence, to mine global in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formation in medical images, TransUNet [38], TransFuse [39],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: PCAT-UNet [40], and UTNet [41] have been designed by combining

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Transformer and U-Net in diverse ways. These methods [38–41] have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: obtained convincing results. However, they used a transformer model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: directly to achieve global relationship modeling, leading to very com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plex network structures. In addition, the traditional transformer struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture inevitably loses key positional information even with the addition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of position embeddings.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Researchers typically employ a single-branch model to implement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image segmentation in most scenarios. Owing to the natural

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: characteristics of a single network, it extracts only specific pathological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semantics, such as local or global information. As described above, U-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Net uses small convolutions to extract local information. TransUNet

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: focuses on the extraction of global information. Two-branch models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have recently attracted increasing attention in computer vision (CV). For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example, Mobile-Former [42], a parallel design of MobileNet and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Transformer with a two-way bridge in between, leverages the advan-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tages of MobileNet for local processing and Transformer for global

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extraction. It exhibited superior performance in image classification and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object detection tasks. Similar to Mobile-Former, other researchers have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: built two-branch medical image segmentation models, such as W-net

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [43], Medical Transformer [44], DoubleU-Net [45], and S-UNet [46].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: They intend to create bridges" between different branches and fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exploit the advantages of each branch. However, most of these studies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used only two homogeneous networks to generate segmentation models.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, the complementary local and global pathological semantics of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: heterogeneous networks have not been fully explored. To this end, we go

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: beyond the standard U-Net framework and investigate the possibility of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bridging two heterogeneous networks smartly and conveniently to mine

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sufficient pathological semantics and complete medical image segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation more effectively.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To appreciate the capabilities of U-Net, we scrutinized its network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: architecture and identified some core areas for model improvement. To

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: make full use of the global and local pathological semantics in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical images, on the one hand, we embed the ConvNeXt [47] into our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two-branch model seamlessly. As we know ConvNeXt, with an encoding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure, has been successfully used for various CV tasks, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: brain age estimation [48], speech recognition [49], crack detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [50], and breast malignancy prediction [51]. It absorbs the latest

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: advanced technologies of transformers into the traditional CNN struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture and explores the inverted bottleneck design and large kernels. On

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the other hand, inspired by Mobile-Former [42], W-net [43], and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DoubleU-Net [45], we seamlessly bridge U-Net and ConvNeXt in parallel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to mine the complementary pathological semantics between the two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: heterogeneous networks. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: study that bridges U-Net and ConvNeXt in medical image segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Finally, we propose a new multilabel recall loss (MRL) module to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: address the class imbalance problem. We designed a novel two-branch

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model called BCU-Net for medical image segmentation. Here, "B"

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: means bridge, “C" represents ConvNeXt and “U-Net" represents U-Net.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We validated BCU-Net using six medical image datasets. Extensive ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: periments show that BCU-Net has a highly competitive performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compared to the most advanced baselines. This study makes four con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ceptual and empirical contributions:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) We redesigned the original ConvNeXt to satisfy the encoder-decoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure, which is suitable for medical image segmentation and built

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a firm foundation for BCU-Net. To the best of our knowledge, this is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the first study employing ConvNeXt for medical image segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2) We propose BCU-Net, which seamlessly bridges U-Net and ConvNeXt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using a loss function. BCU-Net not only alleviates the class imbalance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: problem but also makes full use of the complementary local and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: global pathological semantics between the two heterogeneous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: networks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3) Extensive experiments on six medical image datasets demonstrated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the effectiveness and robustness of BCU-Net. Notably, BCU-Net and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its variants achieved satisfactory segmentation performance. BCU-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Net code is available at https://github.com/ZX-ECJTU/BCU-Net.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4) BCU-Net is plug-and-play and more flexible. This required fewer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network interactions. Each branch of BCU-Net can be replaced with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other off-the-shelf segmentation networks. More importantly, BCU-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Net has two-dimensional generalization capabilities. First, it works

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on different datasets, including blood vessel and polyp images. Sec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ond, it handles medical images of different resolutions well.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: review existing related research. In Section 3, we present the detailed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: design information of the BCU-Net. The experimental results are pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sented in Section 4. The discussion and conclusions are presented in

layout_dets.text: 2. Related work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1. Medical image segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: With the rapid development of neural networks, encoder-decoder-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based structures such as U-Net [12] have achieved remarkable prog-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ress in the field of medical image segmentation. Inspired by U-Net, an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increasing number of researchers have focused on modifying the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoder-decoder structure to obtain a more satisfactory segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance. Therefore, we must first provide a concise review of this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: study.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Zhou et al. [52] proposed U-Net++ using a group of nested and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dense skipping connections to aggregate multiscale features. U-Net++

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exhibits superior performance for different morphologies, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polyps, nuclei, liver, and brain tumors. Cui et al. [53] embedded a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spatial pyramid pool into skip connections, which helped to acquire

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multiscale features for retinal vessel segmentation. Huang et al. [54]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed U-Net3+ optimize full-size features for liver CT segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Unlike previous works [52–54], Huang et al. [55] and Jha et al. [56]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inserted a squeeze and excitation module into each convolutional layer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to effectively facilitate feature extraction. Rather than modifying the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure of U-Net, other researchers employed diverse losses, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: focal loss [57], joint loss [58], and focal Tversky loss [59], to optimize

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: U-Net. Each loss type addresses a specific segmentation problem. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aforementioned methods [52–59] pay more attention to the extraction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of local pathological semantics owing to the use of a small convolution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Most global information was ignored, which affected the final segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation performance. To alleviate this problem, numerous multiscale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dilated convolution modules [60–62] providing larger receptive fields

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been proposed to extract sufficient global pathological informa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion. Moreover, a dual-encoded U-Net (DEU-Net) [63], which uses a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contextual path with multiscale convolution blocks, was designed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieve the same goal. Some researchers have strived to make full use of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the advantages of U-Net and Transformer. Hence, TransUNet [38],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: TransFuse [39], PCAT-UNet [40], and UTNet [41] have recently been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: designed. Owing to the combination of local and global information,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these models achieved satisfactory segmentation performances. How-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ever, they [40,41] are too complex to implement because of the direct

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: application of the transformer structure. In addition, they lose most of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their key positional information.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In summary, most of the aforementioned models ignore global

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pathological semantics in medical images. Although transformers have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been incorporated into recent models [38–41] for global relationship

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modeling, they can be difficult to reproduce. More importantly, they

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: employed only a single branch to complete medical image segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Complementary local and global pathological semantics between het-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erogeneous networks have not been fully explored, which may lower the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: final segmentation performance. Therefore, an effective segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 2.2. Two-branch segmentation model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recently, two-branch models have been shown to play an important

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: role in CV. For example, Mobile-Former [42], a parallel design of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MobileNet and Transformer with a two-way bridge between them, was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed to implement image classification and object detection. Tan

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. [64] proposed a two-branch parallel deep fusion network for 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object detection. Neven et al. [65] designed a two-branch network for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixel-based defect segmentation and severity estimations. Bao et al. [66]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed a two-branch deep network for 3D point cloud classification.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ma et al. [67] combined a multiscale matched filter and a U-net model to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extract vascular features using three channels and fused the segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion results of the three channels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recently, inspired by the two-branch studies above, researchers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduced the two-branch idea into medical image segmentation. Chen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. [43] utilized a bridging method to connect two U-Nets, making full

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: use of the complementarity of the two networks to improve the final

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance. Kumar et al. [68] proposed a dual U-Net architecture using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an improved Swish function for brain-tumor segmentation. Zhuang et al.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [69] implemented two U-Net links for retinal vessel segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Zhuang's model contains multiple encoder-decoder branches and allows

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for more information flow. Huang et al. [70] designed a two-branch

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: U-Net model that allowed one branch to be trained using weighting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: schemes, emphasizing harder examples to improve the overall seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation performance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In summary, these two-branch methods [43,68–70] added too many

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: skip connections between the two networks. This increases the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complexity of the corresponding model and reduces its practicality. Each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branch of these models focuses on the extraction of local pathological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semantics. This significant global information, which is useful for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image segmentation, is partly ignored. Third, the class imbal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ance problem remains a serious problem in current methods. Finally,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: most of these studies tended to use homogeneous rather than hetero-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: geneous networks to create two-branch segmentation models. The im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plicit pathological correlations between heterogeneous branches are not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fully mined, which helps boost the final segmentation performance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These problems inspired us to design a novel two-branch segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model using two heterogeneous but complementary neural networks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The new model should make the best of all types of pathological se-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mantics and address the class-imbalance problem. However, it does not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: require additional parameters, which improves its practicality. Table 1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provides detailed descriptions of the aforementioned studies.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.3. Research motivations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Inspired by Mobile-Former [42], W-net [43], and Medical Trans-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: former [44], we propose a two-branch segmentation model called

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: BCU-Net. Our research motivation is fourfold: First, the local and global

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pathological semantics should be considered. We leverage the advan-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tages of ConvNeXt for global interaction and U-Net for local processing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Second, we investigated the possibility of bridging two heterogeneous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: networks smartly and conveniently to extract sufficient complementary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pathological semantics. Third, we must bridge the two heterogeneous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branches efficiently and alleviate the class-imbalance problem. Finally,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we propose a flexible network structure to reduce the complexity of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed model. Based on these motivations, we propose the BCU-Net

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. BCU-Net

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Problem definition: The medical image segmentation task in this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: study is a type of binary classification task. Each segmented image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contains two types of samples, including foreground objects (we usually

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: use “1" to represent them) and background uncorrelated parts (we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: usually use

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to represent them). Hence, our goal is to predict the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corresponding label map of an arbitrary medical image of size H × W ×

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: C. The map consists of “0" and “1,"where H denotes the height of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image W is the width of the image and C denotes the corresponding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: channel number. Please see Fig. 1 for a more intuitive understanding of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The underlying hypothesis behind our architecture is that the model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can capture fine-grained details more efficiently when the local feature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maps extracted from the U-Net network branch are fused with the global

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feature maps extracted from the ConvNeXt network branch. Comple-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentary learning of the two branches is more conducive to improving

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model segmentation performance. Moreover, following [64,65,68,70],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the two-branch model provides an efficient and complementary fusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model. The network structure of the proposed BCU-Net is illustrated in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 2.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As illustrated in Fig. 2, the BCU-Net consists of two heterogeneous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branches. It seamlessly bridges two heterogeneous networks, ConvNeXt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and U-Net, smartly and conveniently. Traditionally, ConvNeXt is not a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: U-shaped (encoder-decoder) model and is used only for image classifi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cation and object detection. To complete medical image segmentation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we first add a “decoder" part into the ConvNeXt branch, whereas the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: original structure is regarded as the “encoder"part of this branch. Thus,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the redesigned ConvNeXt model can meet the “encoder-decoder'

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure, which is useful for medical image segmentation. Larger con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volutional kernels in the ConvNeXt branch can acquire a relatively large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: perceptual field, which contributes to the capture of global pathological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semantics in medical images. In contrast to the ConvNeXt branch, the U-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Net branch acquires a relatively small perceptual field that contributes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the extraction of local pathological semantic information. Finally, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: final feature map of each branch was input into the MRL module to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: implement deep-level feature fusion. The two heterogeneous branches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complement each other to complete medical image segmentation. Here,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we describe BCU-Net in detail as follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: First, in the U-Net branch, we retained its original structure as much

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as possible because we were eager to determine whether the corre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sponding performance improvement of BCU-Net originated from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: another ConvNeXt branch or a two-branch structure. The U-Net branch

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consists of five continuous downsampling blocks, four skip connections,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and four continuous upsampling blocks. Each downsampling block (U-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Net Block) contains two stacked 3 × 3 convolutions, one batch norm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (BN) layer [71], and a rectified linear unit (ReLU) layer. Each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: up-sampling block (Up-Sample-2) contained one bilinear layer, two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stacked 3 × 3 convolutions, one BN layer, and one ReLU layer. The final

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feature map

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is generated by the U-Net branch and is input into the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MRL module for subsequent feature fusion. The smaller convolution in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the U-Net branch makes the proposed model sufficiently capable of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capturing local pathological semantics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Second, in the ConvNeXt branch, we modified the original structure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of ConvNeXt by adding the "decoder" part to make this branch suitable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for medical image segmentation. Thus, the ConvNeXt branch comprised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: four continuous downsampling blocks, three skip connections, and three

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: continuous upsampling blocks. Each downsampling block (ConvNeXt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Block) contained one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolution, one Gaussian error linear unit (GELU) layer [72], and one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolution. A larger convolution in this branch makes the

layout_dets.text: 4.1. Datasets and data augmentation

layout_dets.text: We conducted extensive experiments on four retinal image datasets:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Another deep-level analysis of the contributions of the ConvNeXt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branch, U-Net branch, and recall loss is shown in Fig. 11. As shown in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 11, the proposed ConvNeXt branch had an evident positive effect on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all evaluation metrics except for the Se metric. Particularly, the polyp

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image dataset achieved more significant performance improvements

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 11. Average performance improvement of each metric, the mean Dice and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mean IoU metrics are only used for the CVC-612 dataset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than the ConvNeXt branch. Similar to the above analysis, the ConvNeXt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branch, with its diverse capabilities in mining complementary patho-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: logical semantics, builds a firm foundation for constructing BCU-Net.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Second, the U-Net branch makes a contribution that is inferior to that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the ConvNeXt branch. This contributed more to the F1 and mean IoU

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metrics, which are important complements to the ConvNeXt branch.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Therefore, an efficient method is required to bridge the two branches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seamlessly; the proposed BCU-Net achieved this goal. Third, the recall

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loss significantly improves the Se metric and makes a slight positive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contribution to the AUC metric. Using this module can alleviate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: class-imbalance problem and make the final segmentation performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more balanced. Finally, according to the deep-level analysis, we ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tained a contribution descent order of all modules shown as “ConvNeXt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: > U-Net > recall loss".

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Notably, several other experiments have been conducted. We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: replaced the U-Net branch with a U-Net++ [101] called BCU-Net++,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which has two model variants owing to the different loss functions (CE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or RE), namely, BCU-Net++(CE) and BCU-Net++(RE). Similarly, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: replaced the ConvNeXt branch with U-Net called BUU-Net, which has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two model variants: BUU-Net (CE) and BUU-Net (RE). A validation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whether our two-branch “bridging" idea is robust for model selection is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: required. These models can also be regarded as variants of the BCU-Net.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The corresponding experimental results for the STARE are listed in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Table 15. Similar results were observed for the other datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As shown in Table 15, BCU-Net++ performed slightly better than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: BCU-Net because U-Net++ outperformed U-Net in most cases. This in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dicates three important conclusions: First, our two-branch “bridging"

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: idea is effective and robust for model selection in the field of medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image segmentation. Second, each branch of BCU-Net can be replaced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with other state-of-the-art segmentation networks, which can further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boost the final segmentation performance. Third, our model variants are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: highly competitive in medical image segmentation tasks, which further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: demonstrates the effectiveness of the novel idea proposed in this study.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Finally, our model and its variants were easier to reproduce, validating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their practicality to a certain degree.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We considered improving the efficiency of the traditional U-Net

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model and proposed a novel BCU-Net for medical image segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We first modified the original ConvNeXt to meet the standard “encoder-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder" demand. We made ConvNeXt suitable for medical-image seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation. We then seamlessly bridged the redesigned ConvNeXt and U-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Net to create BCU-Net. BCU-Net comprises two parallel but comple-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentary network branches. One branch is ConvNeXt and the other is U-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Net. Finally, an MRL module is proposed to efficiently and smoothly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bridge the two heterogeneous branches. This module also alleviates the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: class imbalance problem using recall loss and facilitates the deep-level

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fusion of global and local pathological semantics originating from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different branches.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Extensive experimental results on six public datasets show that BCU-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Net is highly competitive for medical image segmentation. Moreover, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has two-dimensional generalization capabilities. First, it is effective for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diverse datasets, including blood vessel and polyp images. Second, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: handles medical images of different resolutions well. In addition, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ConvNeXt and U-Net branches contributed to improving the final per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formance. An important advantage of the BCU-Net is that it is more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flexible owing to its seamless plug-and-play structure. Each branch can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be replaced with other off-the-shelf segmentation networks to further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improve the segmentation performance. Moreover, BCU-Net is easier to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reproduce and deploy, thereby promoting its practicality.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the future, we plan to make more active interactions (diverse

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: “bridging" methods) between the intermediate feature layers of each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branch. We hope that this optimization will achieve excellent results in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each evaluation metric. We intend to compress BCU-Net using state-of-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the-art knowledge distillation methods [104,105]. This helps to narrow

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the gap between theoretical research and practical applications. Further,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some mainstream domain adaption methods may be used to address the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: “gap" between different datasets, which helps alleviate the data scarcity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: issue.
